commit_message:
urlapi: consume trailing dots after IPv4 numerical addresses

If the hostname is specified as an IPv4 numerical address and it is
followed by a single dot, acccept that as a valid IPv4 and remove the
dot when normalizing.

This prevents otherwise legitimate IPv4 hostnames to have trailing dots.
Seems to match what browsers do.

Extended test 1560 to verify.

Closes #21635

fix_commit_message:
urlapi: prevent a terminal `.0x` component to normalize IPv4

Extend test 1560 to verify

Follow-up to 831a1514843bfa4d4d006627

Spotted by Codex Security
Closes #21652
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix d74c0ada4e31 on top of intro 831a1514843b via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (LogicError): curl's urlapi host normalization code (ipv4_normalize in lib/urlapi.c) can be tricked into accepting and normalizing a hostname whose final component is a malformed hex literal consisting only of the '0x' prefix with no digits (e.g. '127.1.0x', '127.0x', '127.0x.1', '127.1.1.0x') as if it were a valid, fully specified IPv4 address, due to an overly broad 'swallow a trailing dot' leniency check introduced to support legitimate trailing-dot IPv4 addresses (e.g. '127.1.'). Root cause: Commit 831a1514843bfa4d4d006627 (urlapi: consume trailing dots after IPv4 numerical addresses) replaced the previous unconditional 'if(rc) return HOST_NAME;' check after the number-parsing dispatch with a conditional that allows a failed parse to be tolerated when n is nonzero, rc == STRE_NO_NUM, and the cursor is at the end of the string -- intending to permit a trailing dot after the last IPv4 octet to be silently dropped. However this same lenient path is also reachable when the component begins with the '0x' prefix (handled by curlx_str_hex) but contains no hex digits at all, because curlx_str_hex also returns STRE_NO_NUM and leaves the cursor at end-of-string in that scenario. The code did not special-case the hex-prefix branch to reject rc failures immediately, so a hex-prefixed-but-empty terminal component is misclassified as the 'trailing dot was swallowed' case.
